title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
statement_md:
There is an integer array `nums` sorted in ascending order (with **distinct** values) that is possibly rotated at an unknown pivot index.

Given the array `nums` and an integer `target`, return the index of `target` if it is in `nums`, or `-1` if it is not in `nums`.

You must write an algorithm with $O(\log n)$ runtime complexity.

hints.text: At least one half of the array (left or right of mid) is always sorted.
Check if target lies within the boundaries of the sorted half.
If nums[left] <= nums[mid], left half is sorted. If nums[left] <= target < nums[mid], search left; else search right.

editorial_md:
### Optimal Approach: Modified Binary Search
Identify which half is strictly monotonically increasing and verify whether the target falls in that interval.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(\log n)$
- **Space Complexity:** $O(1)$
